[[Hassania Agadir|HUSA]] 2–5 [[Maghreb of Fez|MAS]] |matches = 240 |total goals = 501 |longest wins = |longest unbeaten = |longest losses = |highest attendance = 80,000 (Raja vs Wydad) |prevseason = [[2014–15 Botola|2014–15]] |nextseason = [[2016–17 Botola|2016–17]] }} The '''2015–16 Botola''', also known as '''Botola Maroc Telecom''' for sponsorship reasons, is the 59th season of the Premier League, the top Moroccan professional league for [[association football]] clubs, since its establishment in 1915. The fixtures were announced on 22 July 2015. The season started on 5 September 2015 and is scheduled to conclude on 15 April 2016. [[Wydad Casablanca|Wydad]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[2014–15 Botola|2014–15 season]]. [[IR Tanger]] and [[MC Oujda]] entered as the two promoted teams from the [[2014–15 GNF 2]]. On June 5, 2016, FUS Rabat won the football championship after a 4–2 victory against Mouloudia D'Oujda. The FUS Rabat club won the championship for the first time after being runner-up to the title for 5 previous times.{{Cite news|url=http://www.africatopsports.com/2016/06/05/300990/|title=LE FUS DE total of 16 teams compete in the league, including 14 sides from the 2014–15 season and two promoted from the [[2014–15 GNF 2]]. On 12 April 2015, [[IR Tanger|Tanger]] became the first Championship side to be promoted following their 0–0 draw over [[Youssoufia Berrechid]] in week 27. On 4 May 2015 (in week 30), MC Oujda got promoted to the top flight after defeating US Temara 1–0 in their home match.
